# Use The System In This Order

If you are unsure where to start, use this quick map:

| If you are here | Use this |
|---|---|
| "I only have a rough idea" | `$ideate` |
| "I think the question is real, but I need the literature or data map" | `$discover` |
| "I need the design before I code" | `$strategize` |
| "I need the empirical pipeline and outputs" | `$analyze` |
| "I need to draft or revise the paper" | `$write` |
| "I need tough criticism" | `$review` |
| "I need to audit a formal theory block" | `$review --theory` |
| "I got referee reports back" | `$revise roadmap` |
| "I need a local project dashboard" | `$research-tools dashboard` |
| "I need a local HTML report from quality reports" | `$research-tools html-report [type]` |
| "I need mechanical code checks" | `$research-tools lint [file|dir]` |
| "I am stopping for the day" | `$research-tools checkpoint` |
| "I am reopening the project" | `$research-tools resume-context` |

In the author’s installation, `review this abstract` asks the main session to review it. Use `$review --proofread` to request the independent writing critic. Selecting the named skill also invokes its workflow.

# Daily Cheat Sheet

## Start the day

```text
Use $research-tools resume-context for this repo.
```

## End the day

```text
Use $research-tools checkpoint for this repo.
```

## After a risky edit

```text
Use $research-tools verify-edit 03_code/src/estimate.py
```

# Workflow Skills

| Skill | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `$ideate` | screen ideas, generate research questions, and decide what is worth pursuing | `Use $ideate session on this dataset idea and rank the best research questions.` |
| `$new-project` | launch a whole project workflow | `Use $new-project on this topic and scaffold the pipeline.` |
| `$discover` | interview, literature, or data discovery | `Use $discover lit on school assignment and teacher quality.` |
| `$strategize` | identification design and PAPs | `Use $strategize on this question and rank the causal designs.` |
| `$analyze` | coding, outputs, cleaning, estimation | `Use $analyze and build the estimation pipeline plus output handoff.` |
| `$write` | manuscript drafting, revising, humanizing, style-guide work | `Use $write intro with current-draft mode.` |
| `$review` | writing review, peer review, or critic workflows | `Use $review --peer on the current paper draft.` |
| `$revise` | strategic post-submission roadmap planning, validation, execution routing, and response drafting | `Use $revise roadmap on these reports and the submitted paper.` |
| `$talk` | Beamer-first deck building; Quarto only with `--quarto` | `Use $talk seminar from the current paper.` |
| `$submit` | final submission checks | `Use $submit and tell me if this is actually submission-ready.` |
| `$research-tools` | utilities and maintenance | `Use $research-tools checkpoint for this repo.` |
| `$workflow` | look up the phase, role, or handoff for a task | `Use $workflow to explain the handoff from analysis to writing.` |

# Research Tools Cheat Sheet

| Utility | What it does | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint` | saves end-of-day or handoff state | when stopping work |
| `resume-context` | reconstructs last known working context | when reopening a project |
| `verify-edit` | manual post-edit safety pass | after touching code or build files |
| `lint` | advisory R/Python/Julia/Stata mechanical checks | before code review or commits |
| `dashboard` | local self-contained project overview | after meaningful pipeline progress |
| `html-report` | local self-contained report from quality reports | when sharing review, strategy, code, or literature outputs |
| `doctor` | checks installed skill metadata, routes, roles, and voice files in the author’s installation | after changing the live configuration |
| `context` | quick session-status summary | when you feel lost mid-session |
| `compile` | build paper or talk outputs | after manuscript edits |
| `validate-bib` | catch citation drift | before review or submission |
| `journal` | summarize research log | when documenting progress |
| `learn` | draft reusable learning prompts | when a workflow pattern is worth saving |
| `upgrade` | update infrastructure, not research content | when syncing the starter or user install |

# Agent Cheat Sheet

| Agent | Best for | Usually triggered by |
|---|---|---|
| `ideator` | question generation and early screening | `$ideate` |
| `ideator_critic` | early-stage go or no-go review | after `$ideate` creator pass |
| `librarian` | literature collection | `$discover lit` |
| `librarian_critic` | literature coverage and positioning | after the literature search |
| `explorer` | data search | `$discover data` |
| `explorer_critic` | measurement and suitability of data | after the data assessment |
| `strategist` | causal design | `$strategize` |
| `strategist_critic` | identification assumptions and inference | `$review --methods` |
| `theorist` | explicit formal theory support | `$strategize theory` |
| `theorist_critic` | explicit theory review | `$review --theory` |
| `revision_planner` | revision roadmap planning | `$revise roadmap` |
| `revision_planner_critic` | roadmap critique and dependency sanity checks | after `$revise roadmap` |
| `data_engineer` | cleaning and wrangling | `$analyze` |
| `coder` | scripts and outputs | `$analyze` |
| `coder_critic` | empirical code and reproducibility | `$review --code` |
| `writer` | drafting sections | `$write` |
| `writer_critic` | writing review | `$review --proofread` |
| `editor` | peer review synthesis | `$review --peer` |
| `domain_referee` | contribution and literature review | `$review --peer` |
| `methods_referee` | methods review | `$review --peer` |
| `storyteller` | Beamer or Quarto talks | `$talk create` |
| `storyteller_critic` | slide clarity, layout, and evidence | `$talk audit` |
| `verifier` | mechanics and replication checks | `$submit` |

The [Agents page](agents.qmd) lists all 23 specialist roles.

# Voice Cheat Sheet

In the author’s installation, `econ-intro-writing` supplies the introduction structure and `econ-abstract-writing` supplies the abstract checklist. `$write abstract` drafts from the evidence. `$review --proofread` applies the same checklist during review.

| File | Why it exists |
|---|---|
| `bad_writing_examples.md` | records rejected patterns used in the author’s proofreading checks |
| `core_voice.md` | the top prose authority |
| `voice_examples.md` | examples of your preferred sentence and paragraph behavior |
| `econ_paper_register.md` | field-appropriate restraint and register |
| `style_hierarchy.md` | tells the system what wins when voice files conflict |
| `collaboration_register.md` | optional overlay for joint work |
| `journal_tightening_register.md` | optional overlay for tighter journal-facing prose |

| Folder or file | Role |

# Checkpoint File Format

Default structure:

```text
.codex-state/
  checkpoints/
    2026-04-22T18-30-00Z_end-of-day.json
    2026-04-22T18-30-00Z_end-of-day.md
  latest.json
  latest.md
  resume-context.md
```

Use `.json` as the durable machine-readable layer and `.md` as the readable handoff layer.

# Recurring Prompt Patterns

## Ideation

```text
Use $ideate session on [topic or dataset]. Turn it into ranked research questions, check the closest-paper threat, and tell me whether to pursue, refine, park, or kill it.
```

## Discovery

```text
Use $discover lit on [topic]. Start repo-bibliography-first and then broaden if the frontier is moving.
```

## Strategy

```text
Use $strategize on [question]. Give me the main design, the threats, and the robustness plan.
```

## Theory

```text
Use $strategize theory on [formal section or result]. Draft the assumptions, proposition, proof sketch, and unresolved proof obligations.
```

```text
Use $review --theory [target]. Audit the proof logic, assumptions, notation, and calibration.
```

## Writing

```text
Use $write [section] with [current-draft/joint-paper/journal-tightening] mode.
```

## Review

```text
Use $review on the latest draft and give findings first.
```

## Revision Roadmap

```text
Use $revise roadmap on [review files] and [submitted paper]. Extract atomic tasks, build the dependency graph, flag disagreement items, and give me execution blocks.
```

## Revision Validation

```text
Use $revise validate [revision_task_graph.json]
```

## Revision Execution

```text
Use $revise execute [revision roadmap] and route the approved tasks back into writing, analysis, and review.
```

## End-of-day

```text
Use $research-tools checkpoint for this repo. Capture today's goal, completed work, blockers, important files, and next step.
```

## Dashboard And HTML Reports

```text
Use $research-tools dashboard for this repo.
```

```text
Use $research-tools html-report peer-review for this repo.
```

## Lint

```text
Use $research-tools lint 03_code/src.
```

## Next morning

```text
Use $research-tools resume-context for this repo and tell me where we left off and what to do next.
```

# Migration Cheat Sheet

| If upstream Clo-Author says | In Dittonomics use |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | `AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS.override.md` |
| `.claude/rules` | active workflow references and repo overlays |
| slash commands | explicit named skills such as `$review` |
| `.claude/agents` | Codex custom agents |
| hidden hooks | explicit `checkpoint`, `resume-context`, and `verify-edit` |

# One Sentence To Remember

> Call the workflow skill you need, let Codex orchestrate the agent layer, and use the website as the working cheat sheet.
